question: Should Browser CLI `--fields-file` become a hard-capped 1 MiB input, or should the memory-safety fix preserve existing larger valid files through a different bounded/streaming design?
rationale: The implementation changes the accepted input set; code review cannot determine whether breaking existing large form descriptors is an intended public CLI contract.

options.title: Preserve existing file acceptance
options.body: Use a bounded-memory parsing or validation approach that avoids arbitrary whole-file buffering without rejecting existing valid descriptor files.

options.title: Adopt a documented hard cap
options.body: Keep the 1 MiB rejection only after a Browser owner explicitly accepts the compatibility break and specifies the supported path for larger descriptors.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing file acceptance
recommendation.body: Use a bounded-memory parsing or validation approach that avoids arbitrary whole-file buffering without rejecting existing valid descriptor files.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only concrete person tied to the current implementation in the supplied history; current-main Browser ownership needs confirmation.
